chapter: Radio, Jazz Record and Blue Note (Reel 2)
title: Leonard Feather falls out with Hodes over Duke Ellington records
summary: Hodes says he played only the Hot Five, Hot Seven and Bessie Smith era on the show, and Feather came in with Ellington records. They discuss Feather working for Duke while writing as a critic.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Leonard Feather, the critic, and I fell apart. Because he came up to that station with Duke Ellington records. And I had a very narrow -- as honestly as I can be now -- approach to what I thought my role of promoting jazz was. I say narrow from the standpoint of where I sit now. It wasn't bad, I believed in it, I believe in it now. But it was very close. It had to be the Hot Five's, the Hot Seven's, Bessie Smith, James P. Johnson, Fats Waller -- that era of jazz.
And I loved Duke, I collected Duke. But I didn't think he needed my help, and I think that music did.
But he was also working as a critic.
Working as a critic. And this always later on disturbed me very much.
This is to me unethical. Gleason did the same thing later.
